title: Start here
subtitle: One row below is one card
body:
## A row is a card [1]{blue}

The table underneath holds the words. This page holds the design. libelli prints **one card per row** — four rows, four cards.

- Page through them with the arrows under the sheet.
- Nothing here is uploaded. It all stays in this browser.

## Try it

- Change *Start here* in the table. This title changes as you type.
- Scan the code in the corner to open libelli on your phone.

These four cards are the tour. Read them, then type over them — they are only sample rows, and nothing here is precious.

title: The table below
subtitle: Change a cell, watch the card
body:
## Columns are fields [2]{blue}

The header of each column is its name. A box on the page asks for a field *by that name*, so renaming a column carries the design with it instead of breaking it.

- Click a header to rename it. The card keeps rendering.
- Click `+` to add a row, and you have another card.

## The empty cell

This row's `link` cell is blank, which is why **the code in the corner is missing here** and present on the other three. A box set to Hide When Empty takes its space with it rather than leaving a hole.

- Compare this footer with card 1's.

title: The card above
subtitle: Drag anything. Nothing is stuck.
body:
## Move things [3]{blue}

Every box is dragged in millimetres from the trim edge, so the page size can change underneath a design without moving anything on it.

- Drag a box. Grab a corner to resize it.
- Grid and Bounds, bottom left, decide what it snaps to.

## What the marks mean

- [⚠]{red} A red corner means the words are longer than the box, and the rest is being cut off.
- [⚠]{blue} A box can take its top from the box above instead of its own position — which is why this text moves down when a title runs to two lines.

Try it: make this card's title very long, and watch everything below it give way.

title: Getting it out
subtitle: Paper, picture, or the template
body:
## To paper [4]{blue}

1. Press **Print**, or Ctrl/Cmd+P.
2. Check the preview — it shows every card, and you can untick any you do not want.
3. Set your printer to the same paper size as the page, and turn on background graphics.

## Other ways out

- **PNG** saves one card as a picture, at print resolution.
- **Export** saves the design as a small file you can send to someone. It carries the layout, not the data.
- **Export CSV** saves the words on their own.

Press and hold *Import CSV…* to bring these four cards back at any time. Scan the corner for the source code.
